agents write the code now.

a pattern builders kept describing last week: there are more software engineers than in 2025 and demand is growing, those engineers have never worked harder, and agents write close to 100% of the code. the part that should stop you: the bottom line at the companies employing them has mostly not moved.

automating one stage of a system creates friction somewhere else. the bottleneck does not disappear, it relocates. code got cheap, so the constraint moved to deciding what to build, reviewing what came back, and integrating it into something that ships.

the quality side got put bluntly too: the models now produce more coherent architecture than an average engineer, partly because they hold far more context at once. calling it vibe coding undersells it. it is closer to precision engineering, and the precision has to come from the spec.

the default that costs you: measuring the win at the stage you automated. faster generation is real, and it is the wrong metric if the review queue doubled.

what I do: map the whole chain before touching any one link. where does work wait, who approves what, what gets rebuilt twice. then automate the stage that moves the end number, which is usually review or spec and rarely generation.

I use a prompt for this that runs a precision interview on the problem first and only then applies the frameworks, so you fix the real constraint instead of the loud one.

demand for software engineers is higher in 2026 than it was in 2025.

I’m starting a new early-stage AI fund, doing what I love: partnering with founders from company formation on bold bets, long before consensus.

The fund’s LPs will include Sequoia, Jeff Dean, Sachin Katti, Philip Wong (my Stanford professor and Chief Scientist adviser to TSMC), and others whose work has shaped our industry and how I think about AI’s future.

I’ll remain a partner at Sequoia and keep serving on my boards on Sequoia’s behalf.

Sequoia has been my home for the past 11 years. I joined as the youngest investor the firm had ever hired. I grew up here. Through years of intense debate and shared work, I found lifelong mentors and friends who took me under their wing and taught me this craft. They taught me to aim high and take big swings. I’ll carry that into what I build: outsized ambition, relentless truth-seeking and curiosity, and a refusal to become complacent.

Working alongside founders has made me want to build something of my own: a firm shaped from day one around the convictions I’ve developed over the past decade.

Life has taught me not to take time for granted. This is how I want to spend mine.

Why now

We’re seeing a new way of building companies in today’s AI era. Research and products often advance together. A breakthrough can open a market or accelerate a business far faster than expected. Some companies require extraordinary capital and compute early on. Others reach meaningful scale with remarkably small teams. The rules for how big these businesses can get, and how fast, are being rewritten.

But early on, the technology is unproven, the resources required enormous, and the vision seemingly implausible.

This is what I love most: seeing the potential right from the beginning, and helping founders realize their full scale of ambition.

More than ever, it starts with an extreme willingness to believe early, with bold, independent conviction in a founder’s technical insight before any product or market validation. Then, it means helping founders take the biggest swings, giving the rare, long-term patience to see those bets through uncertainty, ambiguity, and turbulence, and serving as a level head when the stakes are highest.

I learned this kind of partnership at Sequoia. It’s the foundation of the firm I’m building.

Believing before consensus

My fascination with AI’s potential took root at Stanford in the early-to-mid 2010s, studying computer science and working in Andrew Ng’s lab. The friendships I formed connected me to a community whose people and ideas would help shape modern AI and build some of our generation’s defining companies. What stayed with me was the gap between what those people saw was possible and what the wider world could imagine.

I’m drawn to founders pursuing ambitions that sound impossible today.

I start with a simple question: “What if everything goes right?”

Then we work backward together to make it happen.

In 2023, Deepak and Abhinav set out to build a general-purpose robot brain at @SkildAI, before physical AI was a consensus bet. Their sim-to-real breakthroughs gave me conviction where earlier robotics approaches had fallen short. But the data flywheel required deployment at scale. We made commercialization as urgent as research and brought in strategic partners like NVIDIA and SoftBank to support the ambition. Three years in, Skild is advancing the frontier of physical AI with nine figures in annualized revenue.

In 2024, Ioannis and Misha founded @reflection_ai with an insight into scaling reinforcement learning. As that grew into the ambition to build a Western frontier lab for open models, the hard question was how a startup competes with labs spending tens of billions. An introduction to NVIDIA and many compute calls and recruiting events later, the team has built Beam, now one of the leading US open models.

In 2025, Anna and Azalia, the co-creators of AlphaChip, founded @RicursiveAI to design models and hardware together. From day one, we made early customers and ecosystem partners a priority. Today, they are showing order-of-magnitude improvements on real workloads, working with some of the industry’s most consequential players, and reaching a defining inflection point.

The ambition keeps growing as these companies scale.

@linear has always had a kind of magic to it. Now it’s the system a new generation of AI companies builds on, for teams and agents alike.

@tavus saw early that we’d one day talk to AI the way we talk to each other. Today, it’s building the human computing interface for a world of AI colleagues.

@Mach_Industries began as hydrogen experiments in an MIT dorm room. It has since become one of the most exciting next-generation defense companies.

Making the ambition possible

Being a first believer is only the beginning. Compute falls through. A deep-pocketed incumbent makes your mission its top priority. A breakthrough changes the opportunity and the capital required overnight.

These are stomach-churning moments, and early belief carries a responsibility to help make the bet work.

This is the partnership I love: turning the full ambition into concrete steps. Raising capital, securing compute and strategic partners, recruiting exceptional people, and winning the first customers together. Thinking several moves ahead while solving what’s in front of us. And as breakthroughs open new possibilities, helping founders dream even bigger.

Thank you

To the founders I’ve worked with: thank you for trusting me and Sequoia to be your first partner and first believer. It’s been the joy of a lifetime, and I can’t wait to keep building together.

Thank you to Alfred and Pat for your leadership of Sequoia and your support of my next chapter. To Roelof, for bringing me into Sequoia and believing in me from the beginning. Alfred and Roelof, you have been mentors in investing and in life. So much of what I know, and the investor I’ve become, comes from your guidance and generosity over the years. To Bill, for the close partnership and wealth of knowledge, always wrapped in humility. To Shaun, for showing me how to think deeply and imaginatively. To Michael Moritz, for inspiring 22-year-old me to dream big. To Doug, for teaching me to keep things simple. To Bogie and Jess, for bringing joy to the everyday and perspective on what matters. And to all my Sequoia teammates, for the friendship, camaraderie, and lessons I’ll carry with me.

To my family, especially my husband and my brother, who have each started companies of their own: thank you for giving me the courage to take this leap.

Let’s get to work!

text:
旧金山聚变公司 Marathon Fusion 称用中子把水银变成了金子，金价不会受影响，他们真正要卖的是抗癌药原料

Marathon Fusion 是旧金山一家 28 人的创业公司。10 月 21 日，公司在 X 上发帖说，上个月他们用核聚变产生的中子，把水银（汞）变成了稳定的金子，速度是欧洲核子研究中心 CERN 2025 年纪录的 10 倍。

先回答最实际的问题：金价会跌吗？不会。

按 Marathon 自己 2025 年论文的算法，一座吉瓦级的聚变电站外面包一层水银，每年能顺带产约 2 吨金子。2025 年全球金矿产量约 3672 吨，要追上这个数，得建 1800 座这样的电站，而眼下一座都没有。Marathon 自己的装置功率是 1 千瓦，只有吉瓦的百万分之一。

这样产出的金子还混着放射性，联合创始人 Adam Rutkowski 去年对英国《金融时报》说，要存放 14 到 18 年才完全安全。

这次实验本身的量也小。CERN 那项纪录是对撞机里铅原子核擦肩而过、被打掉 3 个质子变成的金，2015 到 2018 年四年一共约 29 皮克，不到一克的三百亿分之一，最快时每秒约 8.9 万个原子。

Marathon 说的是“高速率”，比的应该是每秒产量，但公司没说比的是哪个数，也没公布一共做出多少金子、纯度多高。外媒指出，帖子里的证据只有一张伽马射线能谱图，目前没有第三方验证。

原理物理学家早就知道。氘和氚两种氢聚变时，每次反应都会甩出一个速度极快的中子。这个中子撞进汞-198，会顺带再撞出一个中子，剩下的汞-197 过几天自己衰变成金-197，也就是首饰里那种金。普通核电站里这么快的中子很少，聚变装置每反应一次就有一个。

那一家聚变公司为什么要炼金？答案在钱上。

Marathon 今年 2 月发了一篇论文，给每一个聚变中子算了价钱：拿去发电，按每度电约 0.1 美元算，一个中子值约 3×10⁻²⁰ 美元；拿去炼金，值 2.6×10⁻²⁰ 美元，跟发电差不多；拿去做钼-99，值 2.6×10⁻¹⁷ 美元，接近发电的一千倍；拿去做抗癌药原料锕-225，值约 10⁻¹⁰ 美元，是发电的 30 亿倍左右。

这个账决定了聚变装置多早能赚钱。论文算出，只卖电的聚变电站，等离子体放出的能量要达到加热它所用能量的 10 到 22 倍才能回本，现有实验装置离这个门槛还很远。如果同时卖电和金子，门槛降到 3 倍左右。如果专做钼-99，放出的能量只有投入的千分之一也能赚钱。

钼-99 衰变出的锝-99m 是核医学检查里用得最多的显像剂，约八成的核医学扫描靠它，现在主要靠全球少数几座研究用反应堆裂变铀来生产。Marathon 去年 12 月的论文估计，一台 3 兆瓦、远达不到能量回本的聚变装置，就能满足全世界的钼-99 需求。

锕-225 更稀缺。它用于靶向放射治疗：把放射性原子挂在能认出癌细胞的药物分子上，送到肿瘤旁边近距离照射。这类药的市场在长，诺华的前列腺癌药 Pluvicto 2025 年卖了约 20 亿美元。锕-225 长期主要靠美国橡树岭国家实验室从冷战时期留下的核材料里慢慢提取。Marathon 官网写的路线是用聚变中子轰击镭-226 来生产它。

这次帖子里，公司说已经做出第一批医用同位素：用聚变中子轰击锌，得到铜-64 和铜-67。铜-64 用于 PET 扫描找肿瘤，铜-67 用于治疗。产量没有公布。

所以 Marathon 的计划分两步：先用小装置卖医用同位素，以后再靠金子给大型聚变电站补贴收入。论文估计全球黄金市场每年约 7000 亿美元，足够支撑约 2 太瓦（2000 吉瓦）的聚变发电。这些都是公司自己的模型，还没有一笔真实销售。

为了产够中子，Marathon 说要每秒把一万亿个中子打进一个 1 厘米大小的靶子，连续好几年。他们正在旧金山建的装置用加速器把氘离子打到含氚的锂靶上，用途是产中子，不发电。公司的目标是从现在起每月把功率密度翻一倍，这是计划，还没有实际记录。

帖子里还提到，上周他们在“全球最强的等离子体离心机”里富集了同位素，打破了苏联保持 40 年的纪录。这种离心机让带电的气体高速旋转，重的同位素甩到外圈，轻的留在中间。汞-198 只占天然汞的一成左右，炼金前得先这样挑出来。公司没说打破的是哪项纪录、数值是多少。

Marathon 成立于 2023 年，由前 SpaceX 推进工程师 Adam Rutkowski 和 CEO Kyle Schiller 创办，种子轮由 1517 Fund 和矿业巨头英美资源集团领投。团队五分之一有博士学位，这条帖子的后半段在招人。

Universal High Income

The most likely outcome

I'd like to share a little about what I've been working on at my new company @ultrametricai with my cofounder @tylerlastovich. We have been exploring how we could automate the startup itself, leaving founders with more time to focus on their exact mission.

Enter our first release of the Open Startup Repo: https://github.com/ultrametricai/ultrametric

A common foundation for transparent automation of the startup. 

After close to 20 years in silicon valley, backing hundreds of amazing founders & startups, being in the trenches of founding Heyzap (YC08), then solo founding @golden, going through 2 acquisitions and working behind the scenes with some of the iconic companies today, I'm witnessing the largest change to how we work I could have imagined - a truly monumental era of creative abundance. 

I believe the next generation of companies will largely run themselves: from operations, code, product upgrades, growth, vendor control & selection, process execution, special situations, strategy etc etc. That leaves founder time for 'the art' at the very niche core: the (currently) unautomatable, the special leaps humans tend to make, and north star setting.

We want founders to go super deep into the main problem they are trying to solve and not get held up doing anything else, from searching for domain availability with trademark checks to setting their company up, to running their processes on autopilot. 

So to help that broad foundational layer for starting and running a company, we have spent around a year exploring how to help founders focus on their mission across different verticals, geos, stages and initial starting conditions.

Our first few attempts at making something useful actually failed as the market and AI was moving so fast; it just got absorbed into the models or other product releases. We saw polsia happen, openclaw, then grokbot, muse, dots, etc era as the astras, fables, opuses, kimis and jevs rolled out. What seemed to have been missing along the way was a common repo to identify, unify, open and normalize all the lego bricks that startups have to interact with (vendors, processes, business logic, law, best practices, surface areas, art of the possible). 

As the number of software vendors blew up, the interfaces to drive them multiplied, the international startup founder blew up as silicon valley moved from a specific location to a state of mind and global movement. Unlimited pre seed funding in unlimited vertical sub markets and permutations has brought us to the age of infinity but we have yet to achieve being able to type into an agent a very simple sentence with very complex implications 'just setup my company and make $1m/m'. We have ended up with a hybrid mismash of computer use, API calls, plugins, shifting surface areas (API/MCP/CLI/plugins/chats/musish futures), and changing model absorption to vendor balance making it an exciting and unstable time. 

As our first step we started to rank all the vendors that startups interface to when going about their journey in terms of how agentically controllable they are via their APIs, MCPs, CLIs etc and computer use compatibility as we are largely switching from a UI driven world to the agentic control surfaces and onto full automation. We have 100 ranking areas you can check out with an overall open ranking here: https://ultrametric.ai/overall

Then we looked at the processes that startups do and how the vendors rank for the sub steps or process as a whole and how this changes across geos. Open processes: https://ultrametric.ai/processes

Then we started to hack on an open repo for startups that would contain all the components we are going to need for a common foundation for founders across the globe even if our gov processes vary so much from Bengaluru to SF or Lisbon to Shenzhen.  The founder spirit is geo-invariant. 

We have looked at special founder/startup situations, the business logic that will make open modules for the startup that we can hack on together, ranked law firms, government services and interfaces, stacks that go well together. We have mapped the law and lore that maps to startups and the schemas that make up the data objects and documents. But also the open documents and the missing gaps. MUCH TO DO.

All the BS processes and fluff work that founders waste their time on needs to goto zero. I want to see more supersonic planes, cancer drugs, seemingly impossible missions done and increase the bang for buck founders have with their funding. 

This is a work in progress and we are keen for the community to come hack on the repo with us here: https://github.com/ultrametricai/ultrametric

Lets get into the structure of the general repo and the visualizations we made on http://ultrametric.ai site with example links: 

- Open rankings: https://ultrametric.ai/overall

- Open rankings example (online payments): https://ultrametric.ai/arena/payments

- Open ranking example 2 (cap table): https://ultrametric.ai/arena/equity-management 

- Open processes: https://ultrametric.ai/processes

- Open process example (Incorporate C-Corp) https://ultrametric.ai/processes/incorporate-c-corp

- Open situations that founders face: https://ultrametric.ai/situations

- Open startup simulator (you can test our different initial starting conditions): https://ultrametric.ai/startup-sim 

- Open modules (e.g. cap table, payroll logic etc - we'd love help improving these) https://ultrametric.ai/open-modules

- Open law (we are interested in how law changes the processes, situations and normalizing this over time) https://ultrametric.ai/open-law

- Open lore (we are interested in the historical lore of startups, the rules of thumb and heuristics that might guide your agent): https://ultrametric.ai/open-lore

- Open fields (we are interested in how the schema for the data connects to the open modules, business logic, open documents and artifacts of each process eg how is a EIN defined?) https://ultrametric.ai/fields

- Open documentation (eg SAFE notes and missing! docs) https://ultrametric.ai/open-documents

We have looked at YC companies as well in terms of which ones do well agentically: https://ultrametric.ai/yc

We are interested in stacks and how people are changing their work: https://ultrametric.ai/stacks

We are interested in what is automatable and where the agentic ceiling is currently and how to push that up in all areas: https://ultrametric.ai/rankings/processes/most-automatable

There is more for you to explore and a lot more coming in terms of how you will be able to navigate business in an optimal way in your chosen surface area; whether you are hanging in grokbot, dots, muse, claude, terminal, chat, or whatever is coming up in this exciting time. 

We have a lot of data to collect, clean up and help agents navigate the vast landscape emerging functionality the entire startup ecosystem has to offer. 

Come join us getting your vendor in, ranked or that access pattern you have wanted or getting the data more accurate in terms of which vendor is best for a process or steps. Or open a module of something that currently cost money that could be free. 

Also come play in our discord for founders and join the chaos (we can solve each others issues including fund raising tips from me personally): https://discord.com/invite/3aHky836qP 

It's time to lift all the boats in the harbor and I'm extremely excited as to what the community of hackers and painters will hack into the repo, what asks they will have and whether we can shift normalization of processes globally, gov agentic interfaces and have common repo for founders that grows over time. I expect a lot of experimentation along the way, bugs and upside...

I appreciate our backers having faith in us as well from @ycombinator with @garrytan to @immad doing a sizable check (congrats on $1bn rev homie) to @darbyw (congrats on Stripe buying @clerkyinc), @drewhouston form @Dropbox and also @pioneer_fund @tomerlondon cto @GustoHQ and hopefully this is 'boring' and complex enough for Charlie Songhurst :> @delingpole @Liquid2V @ivolo from @segment @ryanpowe @sonicaghi of @kong @DellyTamer+ other supporters (@michaelwfrank, Fundamental ventures and if I missed you sorry moving fast!). 

[And don't worry, all vendor rankings are open scoring methods so no favors are being done if someone backed us and is a vendor they have to compete with how agentic and automatable they are just like anyone else.]

PS: we have bugs and many quality upgrades to make but thought better to go out early and fix as a community. 

PPS: we have other stuff to launch we just thought this was a great place to start and have 200 PRs coming out pretty soon but I still want to know what is broken or doesnt make sense or inaccurate. 

Special thanks to current and past team members for getting us here and all the experiments we did you know who you are.
